title: Arlec Smart 40cm DC Pedestal Fan With Remote $99 + Delivery ($0 C&C/ in-Store/ OnePass) @ Bunnings Warehouse
body:
Deal: Arlec Smart 40cm DC Pedestal Fan With Remote $99 + Delivery ($0 C&C/ in-Store/ OnePass) @ Bunnings Warehouse

[jv] Arlec Smart 40cm DC Pedestal Fan With Remote $99
Get the AI version…
Nothing better than a Smart Arlec…
[Elyxar] AI isn't all that smart from what I've observed.
[Elyxar] Says 36W. Click digital non DC says 50W so not a huge saving $99-$55. Lower noise is good unless it comes with the squeak/tick that a previous model had (I bought one despite the reviews and it went away after a few months). It will take a long time (probably longer than the life of the fan) to make up for that extra $44 you're paying. Unless you really need the connectivity or money means little then AC is fine or look for a cheaper less featured DC fan.
[brocky2006] Not sure on this one, bought one last year and it was noisier than our old kmart specials. Returned them the next day.
Only bought for quiet fan in bedroom. Got one of the shark dc fans instead
[kbw] DC fans use far less power at low settings, the 36W rated figure will be it running at 100%. AC will never be able to run at low speeds so it's not a like-for-like comparison.
[Averell] I have a Ryobi hybrid fan. I'm not sure whether it's DC or AC, but it's noisy, and has only 2 speeds. I guess it's DC, because the AC-DC converter should be much cheaper than an inverter (DC-AC)
[The Hobo] The biggest advantage to DC fans is that they can run on very low speeds. I've always found that speed 1 on an AC fan is too fast for a bedroom (unless it's super hot)
Not sure how much power you're genuinely going to save by going DC, especially when you factor in the initial buy cost. But for the speed control alone, I recommend DC fans, and have 3 at our house, looking for a fourth soon.
The Xiaomi ones are great, and some have built in batteries, which has come in handy for the occasional power outage during summer.
[Dunnymeister] We've put Vornado DC fans in rooms that aren't really suitable for ceiling fans. I've connected them to Meross Smart Power points and imported them as Matter devices in Home Assistant. They're automated to turn on when the room heats up and turn off when it cools down and it's really made a difference to our power bills and overall comfort.
This fan is compatible with Grid Connect, which means the device should work with the Tuya app, which means you can use the Home Assistant Tuya Bridge to set up a similar automation.
I'm considering getting one as a fan when using Zwift/indoor cycling and having turn on automatically (and maybe change fan speed) based on HRM. Like a DIY Wahoo Kickr Headwind.
[JJlikes2eat] GL with the indoor trainer project. I've heard ppl try this before and would be keen to hear your experience.
[turk182] Nothing beats " hey google set fan speed to 9" on a hot summer night while your half asleep
[Series4Episode10] Purchased an Arlec 12v with an inbuilt lithium battery barrel fan about 6 yrs ago … didn't last long out of warranty … Not cheap - NEVER again with their crap!
[kiwizz] Grabbed an open box model for $70 and setup with local tuya on home assistant, works well. Quiet too.
[Climpton] Im looking for a fan that does the job for hot days, should i get this one or is there a better one? Why are people buying this when there are cheaper ones?
